subject: Temporary rate uplift & overage discount for launch - SparkShop
messages:
From: Alex Park <alex@sparkshop.ai>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai>
Cc: Danny Li <danny@sparkshop.ai>
Date: Mon, 4 May 2026 15:08:00 -0700
Subject: Launch next week — short window rate/limit question

Hi Hannah,

Quick note as we ramp toward our feature launch on Friday. Our traffic forecast shows an anticipated 3x spike for ~18 hours (spike window: 2026-05-08 13:00 - 2026-05-09 07:00 UTC). Our current quota will throttle us and we need a short-lived rate increase (roughly 2x qps and a higher token ceiling) to keep latencies stable for users.

Two asks:
- Can Redwood temporarily raise our rate limit and quota for that window?
- If so, what does overage pricing look like for a one-off uplift? We're hoping for a modest one-time discount on burst/overrun charges if we can commit to a follow-up capacity conversation afterwards.

Attached is our traffic forecast and a minute-level spike test we ran. We expect ~45M generated tokens during the 18-hour window, with a peak QPS that would be ~2x our current committed throughput.

We can sign a PO quickly if needed — please advise next steps and any docs you need to get this approved.

Thanks,
Alex Park
Head of Platform
SparkShop

Attachment: sparkshop_launch_forecast.csv (csv, 34KB)

From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Park <alex@sparkshop.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 4 May 2026 17:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Launch next week — short window rate/limit question

Hi Alex —

Thanks for the heads up and for sending the forecast. We can support a temporary uplift for the 18-hour window; there are two ways we typically handle this:

Option A — Time-bound quota uplift (recommended)
- Temporary increase to committed qps and quota for the exact window.
- Billing: provisional uplift charged at our standard per-million-token rate, with a 15% discount applied to the incremental tokens consumed during the uplift window.
- Needs PO or written approval from SparkShop by 2026-05-06 23:59 UTC so we can pre-provision capacity.

Option B — Soft cap with overrun true-up
- Keep current quota but raise soft cap and allow overrun.
- Billing: overrun tokens billed at 1.5x standard rate, with a cap on total uplift spend we can negotiate.

From an operational perspective we prefer Option A for predictability. If you can confirm which option you prefer and share a PO (or permission to generate a DocuSign), I will loop in finance and operations to lock the window and routing.

One quick technical note: if SparkShop plans to rely heavily on prefix caching to reduce per-token work, let us know — that can reduce charges and improve latency.

Looping in Ben for commercial terms and Laura for PO/payment path.

Best,
Hannah Schmitt
Senior Sales Engineer
Redwood Inference

Alex / Hannah —

Thanks for the details. From a commercial view here's what I can commit to quickly so you can close internal approvals:

- We will provision a time-bound uplift for the window you specified (start/end timestamps to be confirmed).
- Commercial terms (provisional): incremental tokens during uplift billed at our standard hosted generation rate ($12 per million tokens) with a 15% uplift discount on the incremental portion (net $10.20 / M).
- If total incremental consumption exceeds 60M tokens, we agree to an additional 5% rebate on the overage portion.
- We will cap total uplift spend to $7000 unless you authorize higher.

Next steps for execution:
1) SparkShop signs the provisional PO (I can attach a template).
2) Laura will provision billing and confirm whether we can route through a committed invoice or apply as a standalone charge.
3) Hannah will confirm the exact uplift window and ops pre-provisioning.

If that looks reasonable we can ship a DocuSign by EOD and pre-warm capacity.

Ben

Hi Ben, Hannah —

This is great, thanks. We accept Option A and the provisional commercial terms you outlined; please proceed with DocuSign and I will route the PO on our side immediately.

Two asks before signing:
1) Can you confirm the exact start/end UTC timestamps for the uplift once you've pre-provisioned? We want to synchronize our traffic shaping.
2) Security: we use short-lived KV caches for prompt prefixes. Can you confirm there are no additional charges for KV cache usage during the uplift (just the generated token charges)?

If you can confirm those two points I will sign as soon as DocuSign arrives.

Thanks,
Alex
